profile: PostgreSQL 16.6 and 17.2 under the pinned native projection and ordinary DELETE profiles.
scope: The ordinary DELETE target can return ordered int4 columns from rows that actually undergo deletion. Analysis admits direct target references, aliases, and closed target wildcard expansion.

Mutation/ReturnedColumn.role: One result position reading the affected target row.
Mutation/ReturnedColumn.structure: One ColumnReference in occurrence zero and one resolved result Identifier.
Mutation/ReturnedColumn.conditions: The field fixes the occurrence. The owning DELETE validates the field's slot in the target layout before publication.
Mutation/ReturnedColumn.meaning: Read the selected int4 field from the deleted row and name this result position.
Mutation/ReturnedColumn.externalInterpretation: Use the same resolved target relation, declared int4 field, native profile and deletion behavior.
Mutation/ReturnedColumn.sql: Emit the exact quoted target column followed by its explicit quoted output label.

composition: Delete owns an empty or ordered list of at most 1024 checked fields. An empty list preserves command-only output. Every returned slot belongs to the selected target occurrence. The target retains only its absolute name, used int4 column names and descendant policy. The output list may repeat slots or labels. The same DELETE predicate and trigger behavior apply with or without RETURNING.

predecessorCheck.reason: The previous witness is explicitly required as a positive analyzed case in this revision. The unsupported-clause boundary remains mandatory and the USING witness has a resolved control declaration. MySQL retains its LIMIT witness.

observations: Compare physical post-state and restoration, command row count, trigger rows, ordered result names and int4 types, exact returned values, NULL and row multiplicity.
The returned row bag has no guaranteed order. Column positions and duplicate labels remain significant even when the database produces zero rows.
The fixture has an inherited child with distinct and duplicate data, an unrelated control table, NULLs and repeated parent rows. An AFTER DELETE trigger logs each affected physical row.
The native engine evaluates the RETURNING list against the deleted row. Triggers, privileges and server data remain evaluation conditions.

finite.completeness: Measure the product of the two descendant policies, four predicates and six ordered field layouts exactly once each. Recover each identity from the checked value observed by the outer runner.

exploration.structure: Generate one to five output positions with repeated, reordered and distinctly labelled slots, choose between the inherited target and its child, and vary predicates and ONLY.

open: General returned expressions, target column types beyond int4, joined deletes, and newer release output aliases for OLD and NEW.
trust: Native PDO positional metadata, rows and state observation
Independently defined DELETE effects and ordered target slot projection
Exact PHP shape, source identity and construction audit
